requirements.quote:
F:   The contents of frames with this marking are flow controlled;
        see Section 4.
requirements.required_behavior: The contents of the frame are subject to flow control.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame handling can be inspected or tested to determine whether content of every F-marked frame is accounted for by flow control.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST treat the receipt of a frame of unknown type as a
   connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a frame whose type is unknown.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the receipt as a connection error of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send an unknown frame type and verify that the endpoint raises the specified connection error.

requirements.quote:
All frames are idempotent in this version of QUIC.  That is, a valid
   frame does not cause undesirable side effects or errors when received
   more than once.
requirements.condition: A valid frame is received more than once.
requirements.required_behavior: Process repeated receipt idempotently, without undesirable side effects or errors caused by the repetition.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Cause undesirable side effects or errors merely because the valid frame was received more than once.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can be tested by delivering the same valid frame repeatedly and comparing resulting state, side effects, and errors.

requirements.quote:
The Frame Type field uses a variable-length integer encoding (see
   Section 16), with one exception.  To ensure simple and efficient
   implementations of frame parsing, a frame type MUST use the shortest
   possible encoding.
requirements.condition: A frame type is encoded in a Frame Type field.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the frame type using the shortest possible variable-length integer encoding.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a longer variable-length integer encoding when a shorter encoding can represent the frame type.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded width can be compared with the minimum variable-length integer width capable of representing the frame type value.

requirements.quote:
possible encoding.  For frame types defined in this document, this
   means a single-byte encoding, even though it is possible to encode
   these values as a two-, four-, or eight-byte variable-length integer.
requirements.condition: A frame type defined in this document is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a single-byte encoding for the frame type.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode the frame type as a two-, four-, or eight-byte variable-length integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized Frame Type field for each frame type defined in the document can be checked for an encoded length of exactly one byte.

requirements.quote:
For instance, though 0x4001 is a legitimate two-byte encoding for a
   variable-length integer with a value of 1, PING frames are always
   encoded as a single byte with the value 0x01.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode its Frame Type as the single byte 0x01.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the two-byte encoding 0x4001 or any other non-single-byte encoding for the PING frame type.
requirements.why_checkable: The first encoded field of a serialized PING frame can be checked for the exact one-byte value 0x01.

requirements.quote:
encoded as a single byte with the value 0x01.  This rule applies to
   all current and future QUIC frame types.
requirements.condition: Any current or future QUIC frame type is encoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the rule that the frame type uses its shortest possible encoding.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Exempt a current or future QUIC frame type from the shortest-possible-encoding rule.
requirements.why_checkable: For any implemented QUIC frame type, its encoded width can be checked against the shortest width capable of representing its value.

requirements.quote:
all current and future QUIC frame types.  An endpoint MAY treat the
   receipt of a frame type that uses a longer encoding than necessary as
   a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a frame type encoded using more bytes than necessary.
requirements.error_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to treat the receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can send a non-minimally encoded frame type and accept the specified PROTOCOL_VIOLATION connection error as permitted behavior.
